autogo.overview:
AutoGo is an online system that supports car rental services. Customers can browse available cars, make rental bookings for a specific time period, and pay a deposit online. After using the car, customers return it and complete the remaining payment if required.
Staff members are responsible for managing vehicles, confirming bookings, and inspecting cars upon return. The system automatically updates booking and vehicle statuses according to the business workflow.

questions.title: Question 1 (3.0 points) – Class Diagram
questions.text:
You are required to design a design-level Class Diagram for the car rental system. The system is built around a predefined set of classes representing users, vehicles, bookings, and payments. Your task is to enrich these classes with appropriate attributes, methods, and relationships.
In this system, different types of users exist with shared and specialized responsibilities. Customers can create bookings, each booking is associated with a specific car, and payments are recorded for each booking. The system follows the Repository Pattern to separate business logic from data access logic.
Your Class Diagram must satisfy the following requirements:
The classes Customer and Staff are specialized types of User and must inherit from it.
A customer can create multiple bookings, while each booking is linked to exactly one car.
A booking may involve one or more payments, such as a deposit or final payment.
Business logic related to payments is handled by a service class, which depends on repository classes.
Repository classes must implement a generic repository interface.
Your diagram must correctly apply UML relationships, including:
Inheritance and interface implementation.
Association, aggregation, and composition where appropriate.
Dependency relationships between service and repository layers.
Multiplicity, attributes, and methods should be defined clearly and reasonably.

questions.title: Question 2 (4.0 points) – Sequence Diagram
questions.text:
Use Case: Create Booking and Pay Deposit
This question focuses on the interaction flow that occurs when a customer creates a booking and pays a deposit. The process starts when the customer selects a car and requests to make a booking. The system checks the availability of the car for the selected period before proceeding.
If the car is available, a booking is created and the customer proceeds to payment. Depending on the payment result, the booking is either confirmed or cancelled.
Your Sequence Diagram must meet the following requirements:
The diagram must be designed using either Layered Architecture or Microservices Architecture.
The interaction flow must clearly show:
A user-facing component (UI or boundary).
A service or controller component handling business logic.
Repository components responsible for data access.
Domain entities such as Booking and Car.
Repository Pattern usage must be explicit through repository method calls.
Conditional behavior must be modeled using alt fragments for:
Car availability.
Payment success or failure.

questions.title: Question 3 (3.0 points) – Activity Diagram
questions.text:
Use Case: Return Car
This question describes the workflow that occurs when a customer returns a rented car. After the car is returned, a staff member inspects its condition and reports the result to the system. Based on this inspection, the system determines whether additional charges are required.
You are required to model this process using an Activity Diagram with the following characteristics:
The diagram must include at least two swimlanes representing Staff and System responsibilities.
Decision nodes must be used to determine whether additional fees are applied.
The workflow must clearly show the completion of the booking and update of system status.
Start and end points of the activity must be clearly indicated.
You must clearly indicate the modeling level of your Activity Diagram:
Level 2 – Design: Swimlanes represent Actor/Role and Component/Service (detailed).

library.overview:
FPT University Library provides book borrowing services for students and lecturers. To support daily operations, a library management system is introduced to manage the book catalog, borrowing requests, book loans, and fine processing.
Readers search the catalog and request to borrow available book copies. Librarians are responsible for approving borrowing requests, handing over books, and receiving returned books. When a book is returned late or damaged, the system calculates a fine that the reader must pay before borrowing again.
The system does not support inter-library loans or e-book subscriptions.

questions.title: Question 1 (3.0 points) – Class Diagram
questions.text:
You are required to design a design-level Class Diagram that represents the core structure of the library management system. The system involves multiple user roles with shared attributes and specialized responsibilities. Students and lecturers borrow books, while librarians manage the catalog and loans.
A book title may have multiple physical copies, and each loan is associated with exactly one book copy. A reader can have multiple loans, and a loan may generate a fine when the book is returned late or damaged. Business logic is handled by a service layer, while data access operations are delegated to repositories that implement a generic repository interface.
Your Class Diagram must satisfy the following requirements:
Student, Lecturer, and Librarian must be specialized types of User using inheritance.
A Book contains multiple BookCopy objects.
A Reader (Student or Lecturer) can create multiple Loan objects.
Each Loan is associated with exactly one BookCopy.
A Loan may be associated with at most one Fine.
Each Loan has a status (e.g., Requested, Approved, Borrowed, Returned, Overdue, Closed).
Business logic related to borrowing, returning, and fine calculation is handled by service classes.
Repository classes must implement a generic Repository<T> interface.
The service layer depends on repository classes to perform business operations.
The diagram must correctly apply UML relationships, including:
Inheritance and interface implementation
Association, aggregation, and composition where appropriate
Dependency relationships between service and repository layers
Attributes, methods, and multiplicities should be defined clearly and reasonably.

questions.title: Question 2 (4.0 points) – Sequence Diagram
questions.text:
Use Case: Borrow Book
This question focuses on the interaction flow that occurs when a reader requests to borrow a book and receives the book copy. The process begins when the reader searches the catalog and selects a book. The system checks whether an available copy exists and whether the reader is eligible to borrow (e.g., no unpaid fines and below the borrowing limit).
If the conditions are satisfied, a loan is created and a librarian approves the request and hands over the book copy. If no copy is available or the reader is not eligible, the process ends without creating a loan.
You are required to model this workflow using a Sequence Diagram, showing how interactions flow through system components or services based on the selected architecture.
Your Sequence Diagram must meet the following requirements:
The architecture must be either Layered Architecture or Microservices Architecture and applied consistently.
The interaction flow must clearly include:
A user-facing component (UI or boundary, such as Library Portal)
A controller or service component handling business logic
Repository components responsible for data access
Domain entities such as Loan, BookCopy, and Fine
Repository Pattern usage must be explicit through repository method calls.
Conditional behavior must be modeled using alt fragments for:
Copy availability and reader eligibility
Approval success or rejection

questions.title: Question 3 (3.0 points) – Activity Diagram
questions.text:
Use Case: Return Book
This question describes the workflow that occurs when a reader returns a borrowed book. After the book is returned, a librarian inspects its condition and checks the due date in the system. Based on this inspection, the system determines whether a fine must be applied for late return or damage. If a fine is applied, the reader pays the fine before the loan is closed.
You are required to model this process using an Activity Diagram with the following characteristics:
The diagram must include at least two swimlanes representing Librarian and System responsibilities.
Decision nodes must be used to determine whether a fine is applied.
The workflow must clearly show the closing of the loan and update of book copy status.
Start and end points of the activity must be clearly indicated.
You must clearly indicate the modeling level of your Activity Diagram:
Level 2 – Design: Swimlanes represent Actor/Role and Component/Service (detailed).

medicare.overview:
MediCare is an online system that supports clinic appointment services. Patients can browse available doctors and time slots, book medical appointments, and pay a consultation fee online. After the examination, the doctor records the medical result and the appointment is completed.
Receptionists are responsible for confirming appointments and managing doctor schedules, while doctors conduct examinations and write prescriptions. The system automatically updates appointment and time-slot statuses according to the business workflow.
The system does not support medicine delivery or health insurance claims.

questions.title: Question 1 (3.0 points) – Class Diagram
questions.text:
You are required to design a design-level Class Diagram for the clinic appointment system. The system involves multiple user roles with shared attributes and specialized responsibilities. Patients book appointments, receptionists confirm them, and doctors perform examinations.
Each doctor has a working schedule composed of multiple time slots, and each appointment is linked to exactly one time slot of a doctor. Every appointment is associated with a payment, and a completed appointment produces exactly one medical record which may contain multiple prescription items. The system follows the Repository Pattern to separate business logic from data access logic.
Your Class Diagram must satisfy the following requirements:
Patient, Receptionist, and Doctor must be specialized types of User using inheritance.
A Doctor has one Schedule, and a Schedule contains multiple TimeSlot objects.
A Patient can create multiple Appointment objects.
Each Appointment is linked to exactly one TimeSlot and is associated with exactly one Payment.
A completed Appointment produces exactly one MedicalRecord, which is composed of multiple PrescriptionItem objects.
Each Appointment has a status (e.g., Requested, Confirmed, Paid, InProgress, Completed, Cancelled).
Business logic related to booking, confirmation, and payment is handled by service classes.
Repository classes must implement a generic Repository<T> interface.
The service layer depends on repository classes to perform business operations.
The diagram must correctly apply UML relationships, including:
Inheritance and interface implementation
Association, aggregation, and composition where appropriate
Dependency relationships between service and repository layers
Attributes, methods, and multiplicities should be defined clearly and reasonably.

questions.title: Question 2 (4.0 points) – Sequence Diagram
questions.text:
Use Case: Book Appointment and Pay Fee
This question focuses on the interaction flow that occurs when a patient books an appointment and pays the consultation fee. The process starts when the patient selects a doctor and a time slot. The system checks the availability of the time slot before proceeding.
If the time slot is available, an appointment is created and the patient proceeds to payment. Depending on the payment result, the appointment is either confirmed or cancelled and the time slot is released.
You are required to model this workflow using a Sequence Diagram, showing how interactions flow through system components or services based on the selected architecture.
Your Sequence Diagram must meet the following requirements:
The architecture must be either Layered Architecture or Microservices Architecture and applied consistently.
The interaction flow must clearly include:
A user-facing component (UI or boundary, such as Patient App)
A controller or service component handling business logic
Repository components responsible for data access
Domain entities such as Appointment, TimeSlot, and Payment
Repository Pattern usage must be explicit through repository method calls.
Conditional behavior must be modeled using alt fragments for:
Time slot availability
Payment success or failure

questions.title: Question 3 (3.0 points) – State Diagram
questions.text:
Target: Appointment Lifecycle Management
In the MediCare system, each Appointment goes through a series of states from the moment it is requested until it is completed or cancelled. The system must track appointment status to ensure proper coordination between patients, receptionists, and doctors, and to handle cases such as payment failure or appointment cancellation.
You are required to design a State Diagram for the Appointment entity, describing the full lifecycle of an appointment. The diagram should clearly show the states an appointment can be in, as well as the events that trigger transitions between those states.
Your State Diagram must satisfy the following requirements:
The diagram must include a clearly defined initial state and final state.
The diagram must include at least the following states (state names may vary, but the meaning must be preserved):
Requested – the appointment has been requested by the patient
Paid – the consultation fee has been paid successfully
Confirmed – the appointment has been confirmed by the receptionist
InProgress – the examination is currently taking place
Completed – the examination has finished and the medical record is issued
The diagram must include an alternative termination state such as Cancelled or PaymentFailed to represent unsuccessful scenarios.
At least six state transitions must be shown, each with a clear triggering event, such as:
payFee
payFail
confirmAppointment
startExamination
finishExamination
cancelAppointment
At least one branching path must represent payment failure or appointment cancellation.
